Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr (Stepped) pressure build-up tests, (SPBUT) being performed on all (6) wells on the Cappucci pad. The Cappucci 4H, N 2H, 102H, 2H, N 4H and HJMM WYO 1H wells. These tests are being performed to assess the results of the initial remedial deployment of Renegades localized casing expansion tool in the production casing of the Cappucci 2H, N2H, 4H and 102H wells on 12/20/20, 1/20/21 and 1/23/21. This is the 2nd round of testing since initial remedial work was performed. SPBUTs were initiated on 7/12/21 @ ~ 11:00 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - All (6) wells annuli are shut in with the exception of the 2H (9x5) annulus which was opened early and re shut in today at 11:33. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Rep. Tyler Chapman and Creston Consultant Reps., Kevin Leaman and Tom Messing. Starting at approx. 11:30am, ending annuli pressures were checked using a Digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. CALLC will share gas sample results with The Department when received. properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Beech Resources Llc

Violation Date: 2020-06-02
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 885883
Permit API: 081-21803
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lycoming Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-06-02
Comments: On June 2, 2020, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection as a response to a reported production fluid spill at Beech Resources Premier Pad. DEP received a phone call from Don Stevenson with Beech Resources reporting a spill of around 400 gallons of production fluid from the GPU onsite. A dump line valve on the GPU recently failed and was replaced. Within the next couple days vegetation downslope from the GPU was noticed to be dead. How the production fluid was spilled is still being determined. At the time of the inspection, the operator was in the process of excavating the impacted soil. There are two strips of impacted soil, they are about equal in size. The impacted area is about 10 ft wide by 90 ft long. At the top of the slope, the excavator had dug up about 3 ft deep of soil. Soil conductivity in the right strip of dead vegetation ranged from 700 uS/cm to over range readings of the meter, which is 4,000 uS/cm. The impacted soil is still within the LOD so no production fluid left the permitted LOD. Beech Resources plans to follow the Act 2 remediation. The spill of production fluid outside of containment is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), §78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. Outstanding violations from Inspection No. 3001824 still remain.

Comments: Responded to a call from Minard Run to Scott Motter ( Dep representative) in regards that there had been a crude oil spill at one of there tank batteries in Forest County, Howe Township PA. Upon arriving on location I met with Minard Run Representative Gary Davis and USFS Mike Lewis. They gave a brief run down of the incident and work that had been completed to stop the flow of Crude Oil. There was a failure at well 053-27124. A valve broke which was connected to a steel line on the exit side of the check valve, which is going to tank battery. Minard Run is on site. A new valve was installed. Booms and pads were in place at the time of my arrival. They are Currently digging diversion ditches and a siphon dam. Crude product left the well site, traveled the road ditch, and went through a culvert. At that point some of the product went into a fresh water pond and some oil diverted around the pond into a wet land and then into a wooded area. Once it entered the wooded area the product penetrated the large rock structure area and flowed underground to the fresh water tributary. Pictures show where Minard Run placed booms to attempt to stop the flow down stream. The flow is carrying some product further down stream, in which they have more booms in place. It was approx estimate of 2 to 3 barrels of crude leaked. Minard Run was going to try to get a volume of the gathering lines to help identify the volume. It was suggested to add additional booms down stream and continue with the current clean up process. In light of future rains tonight it was suggested to leave booms in-place and remove pads to prevent them being pushed down stream. Minard Run did an excellent job responding and attempting to clean up the oil in the early stages of the incident. This will be forwarded to WQS for follow up.

Comments: On January 6, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an administrative inspection for a spill at the Inflection Energy Hensler Well Pad. On January 5, 2022, around 2140, Zac Subra reported a spill of approximately 30 gallons of hydraulic fluid to the well pad surface. At about 920 on January 6, 2022, DEP spoke with Zac Subra on the phone. Mr. Subra said a hydraulic fluid line on a water truck ruptured and caused the spill. Inflection contractors began removing the hydraulic fluid and excavating the impacted soil immediately. Inflection contractors excavated an area of about 20 ft. X 15 ft. of the pad surface. Due to the ground being frozen, Inflection contractors only had to scrape the top of the pad surface to remove the impacted soil in the previously noted area. The impacted soil was added to a rolloff dumpster and hauled to a landfill. Inflection then went back to the pad during the day to verify that the impacted soil had been completely removed. Zac said a small amount of remaining soil had to be removed at this time since it was not observed earlier in the morning. The small amount of soil was added to barrels and is awaiting approval to be disposed of. Inflection then backfilled the excavated area with clean fill. Photos of the area excavated and clean up were provided by Inflection Energy. The spill of hydraulic fluid outside of containment is a violation of Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Solid Waste Management Act Section 301, and Chapter 78a.54. The violations have been immediately corrected.

Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to reported concerns at the tank battery located near this well.This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack, the well's API number is displayed on the jack. A tank battery consisting of a 210 bbl stock tank and a plastic brine tank within an earthen containment is located beside the well. There is evidence of heavy deer activity inside and outside of the containment in the vicinity of the brine tank. Specific conductance (SPC) of the fluid inside of the containment is near 1000 uS/cm and the SPC of the soil on the exterior of the containment berm is also elevated (~800 uS/cm). This indicates that the fluid released inside the containment has seeped through the containment wall. Water in the ditch just outside of the containment also has elevated SPC (~ 1300 uS/cm). The elevated SPC readings were detected in an approximate 3' x 10' section of the ditch that also has signs of heavy deer activity. There is no apparent impact to the ditch beyond where the deer tracks are present, as SPC concentrations of the water quickly return to background levels.There is currently a minimal amount of fluid in the brine tank, there are no structural issues apparent with the tank or plumbing. I contacted TJ Allshouse and he agreed to an upcoming field meeting to further investigate the matter.Upon discovering the source, amount and extent of the releases at this tank battery, appropriate remediation options will be explored and documented in upcoming inspections. The inability for the tank battery to contain fluid inside of it will also need to be addressed for compliance to be achieved.

Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of produced fluid. The release occurred due to a broken sight glass on a GPU. The exact date and volume of the release are unknown but the sight glass was last inspected on 10/17/24. I spoke with Danielle Schaad, Chesapeake, on 10/29/24 over the phone to get updated information on the remediation process.The GPU was removed and the area excavated on 10/24/24. The excavation totaled approximately 20' wide, 28' long, and 3-5' deep. The material removed totaled about 50 tons. Sampling was completed for Act 2 remediation and the area was backfilled in order to replace the GPU.During this inspection, there did not appear to be any visual impacts off of the pad. Soil conductivity readings were also gathered throughout the area below the pad. Conductivity readings ranged between 0.02 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm) and 0.25 mS/cm. The area will continue to be monitored in follow-up inspections.As noted on the phone call, remediation under Act 2 will be performed due to the unknown volume and duration of the release. The result of this inspection is Violations Noted for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a).

Comments: On August 25, 2025, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to the previous on-site inspection (IR 4031976), the Operator's update that excavation is complete (IR 4036853) and the NOV Response (IR 4036859).Act 9 sign is present. Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is on-site in the mailbox. Well head is tagged. No spills, leaks, or releases are observed at the well at this time. At time of inspection, no personnel from Diversified are present on site, however a crew is on site with earth moving machinery.A soil stockpile is observed along the access road just downslope of the site. The slope below the site appears to be partially backfilled with new soil (Photos 2-5).The rip rap at the culvert inlet was probed for specific conductivity in the same area as previous inspections and was measured to be approximately 7.97 mS (Photos 7-8).Tank is observed in the excavated pit which remains lined with plastic. The plastic appears to be structurally sound at this time.Staining was observed on the access road just downslope of the site and near the soil stockpile (Photos 15-17). The stained area was probed for specific conductivity and measured to be approximately 2.74 mS. The Department could not assess any further as a dump truck arrived on site and unloaded what appears to be new soil onto the stockpile. The Department immediately called Glenn Wilson (Diversified) to inquire about the culvert inlet and the staining on the access road, but the call was not answered so a voicemail was left (12:41pm). The Department then called Heather Empfield (Diversified) and informed her of the Department's inspection (12:47). Empfield informed the Department that she would try to reach out to Wilson and Lisa Raffle (Diversified). Empfield called back and informed the Department that environmental personnel could not be reached at this time but will keep trying (12:53).Excavated areas across the access road appear to remain unchanged since the previous inspection and remain covered in plastic. Empfield called back second time to inform the Department that the Operator is shutting down operations for the day until environmental personnel can be reached to assess the situation (1:18pm). The Operator is voluntarily shutting down operations as the Department did not request or order the Operator to do so. Based on today's inspection, all issued violations remain outstanding.

Comments: On 3/9/23 a routine complete inspection of the McCoy 2 OG Well site was conducted. I was accompanied by Chase Ambrose (PA DEP).During the inspection the following was observed:-A well tag was observed on the wellhead (Photo #1).-The well and operator's information were displayed and visible at the well site as required by OGA 3211(g) (Photo #2). -Some corrosion was observed on the well and production equipment (Photos #3-4). -Two production tanks were present at the site. The tanks and earthen containment berm appeared to be in generally good condition (Photos #5-6).-Freshly placed gravel was observed through the earthen berm containment that surrounded the production tanks. I noticed a small patch of gravel that appeared to be coated in a greasy substance in front of the fiberglass tank. The gravel smelled oily. I used my boot to push aside the top layer of fresh gravel. The gravel below was saturated in greasy fluid that appeared to be pooling below the fresh gravel in the earthen dike (Photos #5-10). -No leaks were observed in the tanks or dump line leading to the fiberglass production tank. -The poly tank was not tied into the well (Photo #8)-I called Bryan Goletz of Diversified and asked him what had occurred at the site. Mr. Goletz informed me that he was aware that an old tank had recently been replaced at the site. I informed him of the spill. Mr. Goletz stated that he did not know that the spill had occurred, and he would look into the matter immediately. Derek Geletko of Diversified arrived at the site shortly after. -Mr. Geletko routinely tends the McCoy 2 well site. According to Mr. Geletko, he had inspected the site last week and did not notice the spill. He did observe that the new fiberglass was at the site at that time. I asked Mr. Geletko if the berm is lined. He stated that he was unsure. -Impacted fluid was observed slowly dripping from the capped outlet drain for the earthen berm onto the ground outside of the berm (Photos 11-12). Mr. Geletko repaired the dripping outlet. I informed Mr. Geletko that I would be returning to the site tomorrow afternoon to follow-up on the spill remediation. Violations of 78.54 and SWMA 301 are being issued for the release.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8181537
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 3/29/2024
Comments: On 3/29/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an admin inspection for the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. This inspection is to report the results of two water samples that were collected during drilling operations from two different locations at the site.During inspection #3724668 conducted on 3/6/2024, the department discovered instances of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad surface and in the sediment basin below the north side of the pad. On 3/27/2024, the department received the results of the samples. Sample 9551-087 was collected from a channel of water along the north perimeter berm that appeared to have a white substance along the length of it. The water field tested at 4.10 mS conductance. The puddle was near the outfall leading to the sediment basin and was approximately 60 feet long and ranged from 6 inches to 2 feet wide and up to 1.5 inches deep. A 2 inch wide by 1 inch deep stream of water was flowing down the outfall that field tested at 4.11 mS conductance. The water was flowing down to the northeast end of the sediment basin. The results are shown in pictures 1 and 2. Sample 9551-088 was collected from the sediment basin where a white plume was visible leading into the sediment basin coming from the rock outfall leading off the pad. The flow of water leading into the sediment basin from the pad field tested at 2.48 mS conductance. The results are shown in pictures 3 and 4.Noted during inspection #3724668, water leaving the sediment basin field tested at 1.156 mS conductance. Water flowing off location field tested at 1.084 mS conductance. During previous inspections, water flowing in a channel below the northeast corner of the pad and below the sediment basin field tested at 0.3 mS conductance or less.The samples show elevated levels of aluminum, iron, chlorides and strontium which indicates the release of a pollutional substance on the pad and reaching the basin.During inspection 3704886 conducted on 1/29/2023, sample 9551-080 was collected from a channel of water along the northeast cornerof the pad that field tested at 4.2 mS conductance. The laboratory analysis of the sample showed elevated levels of pH, calcium, iron, chlorides and strontium as shown in pictures 5 and 6. Bags of deicing media was reported as being applied near this area.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the pad surface and into the sedimentation basin constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code 78a.56(a) and 78a.66(b)(2).This incident has the potential to cause pollution as defined by 25 PA Code 93.6(a), 25 PA Code 93.6(b), and 25 PA Code 91.33(a) and does not meet the discharge requirements under 25 PA Code 78a.60(b).Because of the large volume of elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface and in the sedimentation basin, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3724668 for a 6' x 60' puddle of water with elevated conductance and with a white substance in it; discovered on the unprotected pad surface and flowing into the sediment basin during drilling operations.The DEP recommends the following: 1. The department recommends that Seneca determine the source of the white substance, elevated conductance, pH, aluminum, iron, and strontium in the water sample and take measures to address it, including but not limited to; ceasing discharge, collecting the water for reuse/disposal, etc.2. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid at the north side of the pad and the basin; clean/report as necessary.

Bags of deicing media was reported as being applied near this area.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the pad surface and into the sedimentation basin constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code 78a.56(a) and 78a.66(b)(2).This incident has the potential to cause pollution as defined by 25 PA Code 93.6(a), 25 PA Code 93.6(b), and 25 PA Code 91.33(a) and does not meet the discharge requirements under 25 PA Code 78a.60(b).Because of the large volume of elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface and in the sedimentation basin, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3724668 for a 6' x 60' puddle of water with elevated conductance and with a white substance in it; discovered on the unprotected pad surface and flowing into the sediment basin during drilling operations.The DEP recommends the following: 1. The department recommends that Seneca determine the source of the white substance, elevated conductance, pH, aluminum, iron, and strontium in the water sample and take measures to address it, including but not limited to; ceasing discharge, collecting the water for reuse/disposal, etc.2. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid at the north side of the pad and the basin; clean/report as necessary.

Inspection Date: 11/18/2025
Comments: I was informed by my supervisor that Bull Run Resources had reported a release at their Backwards L #3 well located in Hamilton Township, McKean County. A gathering line failed and an unknown amount of crude oil was released. The release traveled down a road ditch approximately 500 feet heading in a southwest direction to a culvert crossing. The release continued through the culvert heading north for close to 190 feet, before stopping in what is best described as an infiltration sump for the ditch line. The sump contained the release and prevented it from reaching Chappel Fork. JR from Bull Run was onsite with a mini excavator and a lined dumpster that was being filling with impacted soil. He is continuing to work his way down the ditch line removing impacted soil and debris. The sump will be cleared of leaves and debris before being pumped out. Impacted soil will be removed and disposed of at an approved facility. Future inspections will be performed to document the ongoing cleanup. Confirmatory sampling of the remediated area is expected to be conducted when remediation is complete. Documentation regarding the disposal of the contaminated soil is also expected to be provided to the Department.Please acknowledge receipt of this inspection and attached violations by emailing me at ebruce@pa.gov.

Comments: Casey Baldwin (WQS-DEP) and I arrived at the Zick J Pad 1 at 1045 to respond to a spill incident. Jon Sassi (EPS-DEP) was notified by Mike Oakley (EHS Specialist-Coterra) of a release of ethylene glycol discovered at 0738 this morning by a facilities foreman. Mr. Oakley reported that the foreman was on the pad to perform maintenance when he noticed a glycol smell and observed staining on the pad surface near the GPU for the 2H well. The glycol drum inside of the secondary containment barrel was rusted and caused the glycol to leak out into the secondary containment, which then leaked out of the containment barrel through a bung that was not completely fastened, and then onto the pad surface. While on site, Mr. Baldwin and I spoke with David Grosel (Lease Operator-Coterra) who informed us that all wells are temporarily shut in while they relocate the 2H GPU so that the impacted area can be remediated. Mr. Grosel also stated that Resource Environmental was on site earlier in the day to take a sample and would return once the equipment is moved from the impacted area. Mr. Baldwin and I observed the RLE wrecker relocating the GPU while we were on site. We also observed the remaining glycol being emptied from the rusted drum and into a Parrish truck for disposal.Mr. Baldwin and I then called Mr. Oakley for additional details regarding the release. Mr. Oakley informed us that the spill volume is currently unknown as they are still in the process of calculating the volume. He also stated that Resource Environmental will be on site the following morning, 3/19, to take additional samples and remediate the impacted area. They plan to soft dig to remove the impacted material as dump lines are present in the vicinity. On 3/19/25, Mr. Oakley informed the Department via email that the spill volume is estimated to be 47 gallons. The spill volume estimate was determined taking the difference between the working volume in the GPU (384 gallons) and the volume recovered from the unit, the overflow drum, and the overpack (337 gallons).The spill will be referred to the DEP NERO ECB Program for Act 2.Mr. Baldwin and I also performed a cursory inspection of the site. The well cellars appear to be full of fluid. Operator, please remove the fluid, per your plan, before the cellars overflow. Additionally, the vegetated filter strip on the west side of the pad was found to be lacking vegetation and had ruts and tire tracks throughout the area as well as hay bales placed within it. Operator, please rework this area to ensure it is reflective of your plan.Violations noted.

Comments: On January 13 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Aphrodite Well Site (ESCGP issued on 5/9/2020, amended on 2/5/2024, expiring on 2/4/2029) in regards to a release reported to the Department on 1/12/2026 (CTS 394575). Present during the inspection was operator representative Justin Miller.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel.At the time of inspection, there are 5 total wells on the well pad. According to the operator, stimulation for all 5 wells has been completed and they are preparing to conduct drill outs and flowback operations over the next 3 weeks.Upon inspection, it appeared the stimulation equipment was being demobilized. The drilling equipment still onsite appeared to be within secondary containment. The secondary containment appeared to be installed correctly with no tears or leaks. During the inspection, Mr. Miller guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Miller the release occurred on 1/13/2026. He stated the release occurred from a loose hose connection from one of the tanks. At the time of the inspection the operator is estimating a total release of 15 gallons of a produced water was released to the graveled well pad.The Department observed the location of the spill and remediation. It appeared the area of the spill was in an approximate 4 foot by 20 foot area outside of the secondary containment for the tanks next to a GPU. Conductivity readings including several readings of OR (Over Detectable Range, >20MS) , 11.46mS, and 1.57mS, were obtained in the area of the release. During the inspection, the Department observed 2 small areas of excavation. Mr. Miller stated that additional excavation will occur as needed when the containment is removed from its location.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued against the Aphodite 2M well for the observed release.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's Crank O (03-067) well site located in Columbia Township, Bradford County on 2/7/2024 at 1025 hours. The weather was 35 degrees F with partly cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to the DEP by Repsol. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID #378016 is tied to the release in CTS.According to Repsol, on 2/4/2024 at 0840 hours, a spill of approximately 15 gallons of hydraulic fluid was released to the pad surface after a hose on a water truck was found to be leaking. Repsol reported that the release was cleaned up utilizing absorbents and the impacted pad material was recovered and placed in containers for disposal. Repsol reported that no waterways were impacted by the release. During today's inspection, no evidence of any portion of the release remaining could be observed. An environmental consultant was onsite today for proper disposal/removal of the impacted material from the site. Repsol is currently moving equipment offsite and preparing for a workover rig to move in. Silt sock and a gravel berm were installed along the southwestern edge of the pad for sedimentation control (photo #2). Areas surrounding the well pad remain permanently stabilized with vegetated cover or temporarily stabilized with straw. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. No pooled water was observed on the pad surface, outside of secondary containment today.Based on the reported release of ~15 gallons of hydraulic fluid to the pad surface and Repsol's timely remediation of the release, violations of the following are cited as immediately corrected against API #015-23837:CSL 402(b)25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)SWMA 301The 25 Pa. Code 78a.64a(e) violation cited against API #015-23837 on 1/30/2024 remains outstanding at this time.I departed the site at 1100 hours.

Violation Code: 78a81(a)3 - CASING AND CEMENTING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to prevent pollution or diminution of fresh groundwater.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr ¿Stepped¿ pressure build-up tests ¿SPBUT¿ being performed on all (5)wells on the HUNTER pad. The HUNTER 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H wells. These tests are being performed in response to a gas migration investigation in area underway by The Department. SPBUTs were initiated on 5/26/20 @ ~ 08:15 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - All (5) wells on the pad are shut in w/ Frac valves installed on top of well heads. The (20x13) annuli are capped and set up to vent to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and the (9x5) annuli are set up to vent to a temporary poly vent tank via rubber lines. All annuli were closed when I arrived. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Reps. Craig Shores and Trey Sites, Creston Consultant Reps., Tom Messing and Andy Sallaway and D.E.P. OGIS, Ken Kennedy. Starting at approx. 10:15, ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. - The (20x13) annulus vents of the 21HC and 22HC were opened within first 12 hrs. of PBUT due to pressures exceeding 35 psi. These vents were shut back in @ 7 am this morning, check @ 9 am showed pressures over 100 psi. on (20x13) annuli of both the 21HC and the 22HC wells. Op. Rep. bled down these annuli pressures below 30 psi. for remainder of PBUT's. - Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for all the HUNTER Pad wells. - HUNTER 5H: (20x13): 3.0 psi.; 68 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:17 ** (13x9): 277 psi.; 85 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:23 ** (9x5): 327 psi.; 85 % CH4; Sample collected at 10:27 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:20. - HUNTER 6H: (20x13): 17.0 psi.; 65 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:33 ** (13x9): 169.0 psi.; 87 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:37 ** (9x5): 549.0 psi.; 86 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:40 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:40. - HUNTER 22HC: (20x13): 24.0 psi.; 91 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:45 ** (13x9): 226.0 psi.; 89 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:49 ** (9x5): 396.0 psi.; 92 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:52 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:50. - HUNTER 21HC: (20x13): 44.0 psi.; 93 % CH4; Sampled collected @ 10:55 ** (13x9): 268.0 psi.; 90 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:00 ** (9x5): 131.0 psi.; 87 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:07 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 11:00. - HUNTER 23HC: (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 0 % CH4; No sample collected (13x9): 255.0 psi.; 89 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:13 (9x5): 321.0 psi.; 86 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:20 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 11:30. - All (5) wells (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened and venting to poly tank @ 11:45. ** The presence of pressure and gas was detected in the (20x13) and the(13x9) annuli of all the wells on the pad with the exception of the HUNTER 23HC (20x13) annulus.
